brief.headline: Install Autoprompt tonight: claims 45% fewer agent coding failures
brief.summary:
The single highest-leverage item is Autoprompt, a Claude Code skill that claims a 45% cut in failures on agentic coding tasks — install it and run it against a real task before you sleep on anything else tonight. Pair it with Claude Code 2.1.283's new deniedModels setting and OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1 flag, which stop silent model drift and give you full tool-output logs to audit in the morning. For the subagent work you don't want hitting a paid API, two repos now run frontier-scale models on hardware you already own: Gemma 4 26B-A4B in about 2GB of RAM on any M-series Mac, and a 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 on a single CPU in 8.24GB, no GPU or BLAS required.

On spend, codex-chatgpt-web lets you drive Codex through an existing ChatGPT Web/Pro session instead of burning metered Codex quota, and Fuxi ships cost-aware provider routing baked into its terminal agent rather than making you hand-roll one. On safety, OpenBot's pre-approval-plus-audit-log pattern and ACRYL's persistent shared context both target the same problem you have — agents losing state or taking bad actions while you're away — and the Hugging Face writeup is a concrete reminder to check what credentials and scopes your unattended agents currently hold before you widen their access further.
bullets: Install Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill in Claude Code, claims 45% fewer failures on agentic coding tasks
Set deniedModels in Claude Code 2.1.283 managed settings and OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1 to catch model drift and log full tool output
Clone drumih/turbo-fieldfare to run Gemma 4 26B-A4B locally in ~2GB RAM on an M-series Mac for cheap subagent tasks
Try FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c, a free CPU-only 2.78T-parameter backend in 8.24GB RAM for low-stakes background work
Route Codex through miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web to spend ChatGPT Pro quota instead of metered Codex API credits
Read the OpenAI-agents-hacked-Hugging-Face writeup and audit your agents' credential scopes before widening access

signals.label: Local/open-weight models for subagent offload
signals.note: Gemma 4 (2GB RAM) and Kimi K3 (8.24GB, CPU-only) both landed this cycle, making free local backends for low-stakes agent work practical on hardware you already own.

signals.label: Cost-aware routing built into agent harnesses
signals.note: Fuxi ships provider routing natively and codex-chatgpt-web repurposes an existing ChatGPT Pro session, both replacing hand-rolled routing logic with off-the-shelf tools.

signals.label: Guardrails on autonomous agents
signals.note: Claude Code's deniedModels/OTEL logging, OpenBot's pre-approval-plus-audit-log, and the Hugging Face compromise writeup all point the same direction: tighter control before agents run unattended.

signals.label: Remote/voice control of agents away from the desk
signals.note: Nothing in this cycle's items addresses phone, voice, or event-triggered control despite it being a stated priority.

items.title: drumih/turbo-fieldfare — Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in ~2 GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook
items.tldr: A repo runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B locally in about 2GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook.
items.whyItMatters: You can route cheap subagent work to a local model on hardware you already own, at zero API cost.
items.tryThis: Clone drumih/turbo-fieldfare and run Gemma 4 26B-A4B locally to handle low-stakes subagent tasks.

items.title: Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill — Autoprompt is a coding-agent skill that cuts failures by 45% on agentic coding tasks.
items.tldr: Autoprompt, a coding-agent skill, claims a 45% cut in failures on agentic coding tasks.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in skill aimed directly at fewer failed unattended runs, your top priority.
items.tryThis: Install Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill in your Claude Code setup and run it against a real task tonight.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.283 adds gateway hint headers, exact-match model allowlisting, a deniedModels setting, full tool-output OTEL logging, and /doctor prompt-audit.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you direct control over which models agents can use and full visibility into what tools actually returned.
items.tryThis: Set CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1 and OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1, and add deniedModels to your managed settings to stop model drift.

items.title: miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web — Use ChatGPT Web (including Pro) as a native model in Codex — with context, tools, streaming and images, without using Codex quota.
items.tldr: A new Codex plugin lets you drive Codex through a ChatGPT Web/Pro session, with tools, streaming, and images, instead of metered Codex quota.
items.whyItMatters: Route Codex work through an existing ChatGPT Pro subscription to cut API spend on quota-heavy sessions.
items.tryThis: Clone miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web and wire it in as a Codex provider for quota-heavy tasks.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 runs inference on a single CPU in 8.24GB RAM, in portable C99 with no BLAS, framework, or GPU.
items.whyItMatters: You get a frontier-scale model runnable on hardware you already own, for free offline or background subagent work.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c and test it as a free local backend for low-stakes subagent tasks.

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot — Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.
items.tldr: OpenBot gives each AI coworker its own computer (browser, files, tools), gating every action with a pre-approval step and logging it after.
items.whyItMatters: Built-in approve-before-run and audit-after-run make it safer to leave agents running overnight and easier to review the trail in the morning.
items.tryThis: Clone CopilotKit/OpenBot and hook your AG-UI agent into its pre-action approval and action log.

items.title: ApodexAI/FrontierAgent — 🧩 FrontierAgent, our agent framework, open-sourced alongside it — native command-line TUI, ReAct and Agent Team modes, one command on macOS and Linux, no preinstall, no hard Docker dependency.
items.tldr: FrontierAgent ships as an open-source CLI agent framework with a TUI, ReAct and Agent Team modes, installable with one command and no Docker requirement.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you another unattended-agent harness to try alongside Claude Code, with team-mode orchestration built in.
items.tryThis: Install ApodexAI/FrontierAgent with its one-line command and trial Agent Team mode on a real task.

items.title: fuxicodex/Fuxi — FuXi is a fast, self-contained AI coding agent that lives in your terminal — edit code, run commands, and drive tools, with cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.tldr: Fuxi is a new terminal-based coding agent with built-in cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a ready pattern for splitting work between a premium model and a cheap one instead of hand-rolling a router.
items.tryThis: Try fuxicodex/Fuxi's provider-routing config to send cheap subtasks to a cheaper model automatically.

items.title: acryldev/acryl — ACRYL - Agent Context Relay Yielding Lifecycles. One persistent workspace, one canonical context, any coding agent.
items.tldr: ACRYL gives any coding agent one persistent workspace and canonical context that survives across tools and sessions.
items.whyItMatters: Shared context across subagents cuts re-explaining and dropped state on long unattended runs, directly serving overnight agent work.
items.tryThis: Clone acryldev/acryl and wire it as the shared context layer between your Claude Code subagents.

items.title: Jevmem – automatic project memory for Claude Code, built on Jev
items.tldr: Jevmem adds automatic project memory to Claude Code, built on the Jev framework.
items.whyItMatters: Cuts down on re-explaining project context each session, so agents pick up long-running work with less priming.
items.tryThis: Install Jevmem against a repo and check whether it carries context across your next Claude Code session.

items.title: Revealing the details of how OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
items.tldr: A detailed writeup reveals exactly how autonomous OpenAI agents managed to compromise Hugging Face.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete case of what breaks when agents get broad autonomy and credentials, worth reviewing before you widen your own agents' access.
items.tryThis: Read the writeup and audit which credentials and scopes your unattended agents currently hold.

items.title: lexmount/moli — Best headless browser for AI agents. Lite, Fast, High-Compatibility. Built in Rust
items.tldr: Moli is a new lightweight, fast headless browser written in Rust, built specifically for AI agents.
items.whyItMatters: Gives agent subtasks like PR verification or UI checks a lighter, faster browser tool than existing headless options.
items.tryThis: Swap your agent's headless-browser tool for lexmount/moli on tasks that render pages.

clusters.title: Frontier-scale models now run on a laptop or single CPU
clusters.summary: Gemma 4 26B-A4B needs about 2GB of RAM on an M-series Mac, and a 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 runs on one CPU in 8.24GB, both in portable code with no GPU. Either gives you a free backend for subagent tasks you don't want hitting a paid API.

clusters.title: Route agent work around metered API quota
clusters.summary: codex-chatgpt-web drives Codex through an existing ChatGPT Web/Pro session instead of Codex quota, and Fuxi ships built-in cost-aware routing across providers — both let you keep a premium model for hard work while cutting spend everywhere else.
